findings.how_to_check: On machine B, ensure $D_FLAGS/linkage_sample1940.dta does not exist and execute replication/Run-MachineB.ps1 -PreflightOnly; verify that preflight erroneously passes. Grep for linkage_sample1940 across replication/run_machineB.do, replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py, and replication/input_manifest_machineB.md to confirm its omission.
findings.suggested_fix: Add data/names/flags/linkage_sample1940.dta to the preflight list in replication/run_machineB.do and remove the three superseded data inputs. Update EXPECTED in replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py to 15, re-run it to record the SHA-256 hash in input_manifest_machineB.md, and document or script the transfer of the artifact from machine A.
findings.title: The new required sample file is absent from machine-B preflight and input hashing
findings.what_the_code_does: Both table scripts now read local sample_f "$D_FLAGS/linkage_sample1940.dta", but this artifact is generated on machine A and must be manually transferred to machine B. The machine-B preflight in run_machineB.do still checks the superseded ipums_fs_names_for_Deaglan1940.dta, clean_names_1940_new.dta, and divided_file1940_true_cleaned_women_added.dta without verifying linkage_sample1940.dta, and hash_inputs_machineB.py requires exactly 17 data inputs parsed from that obsolete list.
findings.why_it_matters: Running Run-MachineB.ps1 -PreflightOnly on machine B will report that all inputs are present even when linkage_sample1940.dta is completely missing. Once the four-hour table execution starts, linkage_analysis.do aborts on line 63 with a file-not-found error. Furthermore, because the new file is not recorded in input_manifest_machineB.md, the replication package cannot verify the integrity or provenance of the dataset defining the denominators of Tables 5-8.

findings.how_to_check: Run replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do, which already demonstrates on the main sample that kept links (status == 1) cannot change validation status under a single fixed 1940 validator, and decomposes how much of the apparent gain is driven by re-reading vs link selection. Apply the same fixed-validator calculation to the JW and HLINK links.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate both Old and New links against a single fixed human 1940 middle initial (e.g. mi_anc or mi_fs), or explicitly relabel the row as 'Own-Transcription MI Match Rate (%)' with a clear table footnote explaining that the Old and New columns evaluate against different 1940 initial transcriptions.
findings.title: The Old and New middle-initial validation columns change the validating transcription as well as the links
findings.what_the_code_does: For Old links, the code sets miv to mi_anc (Ancestry's 1940 middle initial), whereas for New links it sets miv to mi_ml (the ML model's 1940 middle initial), and computes count if mi1930 == mi1940. The resulting percentages are placed side by side as 'MI Match Rate (%)' in Panel A under 'Coverage and Link Quality' in both the ABE/JW and HLINK tables.
findings.why_it_matters: In linkage methodology, middle-initial agreement serves as an out-of-sample validation of match correctness. By changing the 1940 middle-initial transcription between Old and New, the comparison conflates link-quality improvements with re-transcription differences. Even for identical linked pairs, the validation rate can increase solely because the ML model transcribed the 1940 middle initial differently. Neither the table row label nor the caption informs the reader that different validators are used.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so prose claims and text citations outside the generated LaTeX table captions could not be verified against the code.

The external census, linkage, and truth datasets reside on external volumes (F:, Dropbox) and could not be accessed, and the Stata pipeline could not be executed directly; all runtime assertions and counts were evaluated by static source code tracing.
The review was specifically targeted to the uncommitted working-tree modifications and directly associated replication scripts, not a comprehensive audit of the entire pre-existing codebase.
The selection and independence properties of the FamilySearch-profile truth dataset could not be empirically validated without access to the underlying profile graph and crosswalks.
structured_output.summary: The sample construction and denominator alignments across the ABE/JW and HLINK linkage scripts successfully harmonize with the paper's main table, supported by rigorous record-count and rate assertions. However, the machine-B replication preflight and input manifest have not been updated for the new linkage_sample1940.dta dependency, which will cause preflight false assurances and runtime failures. Econometrically, the reported middle-initial match rates switch the validating 1940 initial from Ancestry to the ML transcription between columns, conflating link-selection improvements with re-transcription quality.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
